215a310c81.text: Every raindrop starts as water on the ground. To fall from the sky, it first has to get up there, and it makes the trip as a gas.

6c3388028f.text: Evaporation is the change from liquid water into water vapour, a gas. It happens when heat breaks the bonds that hold water molecules together.

af664a5a77.text: The vapour mixes into the air and cannot be seen. The water has not gone anywhere: it is now part of the air around us.

4a8abc386c.text: About 90 percent of the moisture in the air came from water evaporating from oceans, seas, lakes and rivers.

664b232a6c.text: Oceans cover more than 70 percent of Earth's surface, which is why so much of that moisture comes from them.

c25167c468.text: Heat turns water into vapour, the vapour is carried up into a cloud, and the cloud can rain on the land.

90221089b5.text: The next lesson follows this vapour as it rises, cools and turns back into liquid by condensation. That is how a cloud is made. You can read ahead in the glossary or go to lesson 2.

c7d0b24423.text: Rain starts as water on the ground.

30e2991736.text: Heat turns it into water vapour, a gas you cannot see.

cd86c1f53e.text: Most of that vapour comes from oceans, seas, lakes and rivers.

91a8d35a93.text: The vapour from the last lesson does not stay a gas for ever. High in the sky it turns back into liquid water, and that is what a cloud is made of.

a3badc7d8f.text: Clouds form because air containing water vapour rises and cools. As the air rises it is under less pressure, so it spreads out and gets cooler.

b7238b755f.text: Clouds form when the air cools below the dew point, and water vapour condenses to liquid water.

52f2eaa167.text: Condensation is the change from water vapour back into liquid water. It is the opposite of evaporation.

b2efdeee85.text: On a humid day, a glass of iced water collects drops on its outside. The air touching the cold glass cools, and its vapour condenses.

72702985a1.text: Vapour condenses more easily when it has a particle to settle on. Tiny bits of dust, salt, smoke and pollen do this job, and they are called condensation nuclei.

2aa8bebb2b.text: Warm, damp air near the sea starts to rise.

c32c7be943.text: Higher up there is less pressure, so the air spreads out and cools.

5e6f8fab1d.text: It cools below its dew point.

f59f67fe30.text: Its vapour condenses on specks of dust and salt.

c991136129.text: Together, the tiny droplets make a cloud.

551889a465.text: A rising parcel of air spreads out and cools. Past its dew point, the vapour condenses into droplets.

8494c3ca26.text: Damp air rises, spreads out and cools.

e47edd8038.text: Once it cools below the dew point, its vapour condenses.

293d02f15d.text: Each droplet forms on a speck of dust, salt, smoke or pollen, and together they make a cloud.

a1789a606a.text: Rain is one kind of precipitation: water released from clouds as rain, freezing rain, sleet, snow or hail.

3d18e47262.text: The droplets in a cloud are far too small to fall as rain. To reach the ground, they have to grow.

1167039f8e.text: Droplets bump into each other and join together, which is called coalescence. Millions of cloud droplets are needed to make a single raindrop.

3542c4995f.text: A drop leaves the cloud once it falls faster than the updraft, the rising air inside the cloud.

42feb8f783.text: When a cloud holds ice crystals, the crystals can grow quickly by taking water from the cloud. This is called the Bergeron process.

87dd9a6c48.text: The crystals may fall as snow, or melt on the way down and fall as rain.

d5831a626e.text: Raindrops are not shaped like teardrops. Small drops, with a radius under 1 millimetre, are round like a ball.

6d5ded5d5c.text: At about 2 to 3 millimetres across, a falling drop is flat underneath, like a hamburger bun.

0ad191a957.text: At about 4 to 5 millimetres, the dip in its bottom grows into a shape like a parachute.

0425ba9834.text: Bigger still, the drop breaks up into smaller drops.

d3aa60a65a.text: As a falling drop grows, air pushes its bottom flat, then hollows it out, until it splits.

693ab32c3b.text: Cloud droplets are too small to fall, so they have to grow.

43ade61d33.text: They merge, and millions of them make one raindrop.

9d97615746.text: In icy clouds, crystals grow fast and fall as snow, or melt into rain.

781630a640.text: Small raindrops are round, and big ones flatten and break apart.
